'''''Elaeagnus multiflora''''', the '''cherry elaeagnus''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''cherry silverberry''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ELMU|taxon=Elaeagnus multiflora|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> '''goumi''', '''gumi''', or '''natsugumi''', is a species of ''[[Elaeagnus]]'' native to [[China]], [[Korea]], [[Japan]] and the [[Russia|Russian]] Far east ([[Sakhalin]]).

==Description==
''Elaeagnus multiflora'' is a [[deciduous]] or [[Semi-deciduous|semi-evergreen]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to {{cvt|2|-|8|m}} tall, with a trunk up to {{cvt|30|cm}} diameter with dark brown [[Bark (botany)|bark]]. The shoots are densely covered in minute red-brown scales. The [[leaf|leaves]] are ovate to elliptic, {{cvt|3|-|10|cm}} long and {{cvt|2|-|5|cm}} broad, green above, and silvery to orange-brown below with dense small scales.

The flowers are solitary or in pairs in the leaf axils, fragrant, with a four-lobed pale yellowish-white corolla {{cvt|1.5|cm}} long; flowering is in mid-spring.
[[Image:Goumi-fruits.jpg|thumb|right|Fruits of ''Elaeagnus multiflora'' in mid June]]
[[Image:Natsugumi & Cigarette JPN.JPG|thumb|right|Japanese ''Elaeagnus multiflora'' var. ''hortensis'', with cigarette for scale.]]The fruit is a round to oval [[drupe]] {{cvt|1|cm}} long, silvery-scaled orange, ripening red dotted with silver or brown, pendulous on a {{cvt|2|-|3|cm}} [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]]. When ripe in mid- to late summer, the fruit is juicy and edible, with a sweet but astringent taste somewhat similar to that of rhubarb. The skin of the fruit is thin and fragile, making it difficult to transport, thus reducing its viability as a food crop.

As with other species in the genus ''Elaeagnus'', ''E. multiflora'' plants are [[actinorhizal plant|actinorhizal]], growing in [[symbiosis]] with the bacterium ''[[Frankia]]'' in the soil. These bacteria fix atmospheric [[nitrogen]], making it available in usable form for the host plant, and indirectly for other nearby plants. This feature allows the plant to grow in poorer soils than it could otherwise.

There are several cultivars, such as Gigantea or Daiougoumi,<ref>{{cite web | title=Elaeagnus multiflora 'Gigantea' | /RHS | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/77438/elaeagnus-multiflora-gigantea/details }}</ref> Tillamook or Carmine,<ref>{{cite web | title=Appreciating Goumi Berry | url=https://www.homeorchardeducationcenter.org/arboretum-blog/goumi-berries }}</ref> Red Gem, Sweet Scarlet,<ref>{{cite web | title=Sweet Scarlet Goumi ™ | url=https://onegreenworld.com/product/sweet-scarlet-2/ }}</ref> Hortensis,<ref>{{cite web | title=Elaeagnus multiflora var. hortensis (M.Bieb.) Servett. | Plants of the World Online | Kew Science | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:3004626-4 }}</ref> ranked here for fruit size which tends to be opposite for taste. Also there have been some hybridization efforts, leading to the JR1 hybrid,<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | title=Le futur du Goumi du Japon (Elaeagnus Multiflora) | date=16 June 2024 | url=https://www.boisderodebos.be/blog/articles-1/le-futur-du-goumi-du-japon-73 }}</ref> with merits on size and taste.

==Uses==
This species is occasionally grown in [[Europe]] (France,Loraine)and [[North America]] as an [[ornamental plant]] and for its fruit. It is an [[naturalisation (biology)|established exotic species]] in parts of the eastern United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=ELMU|title=Profile for ''Elaeagnus multiflora'' (cherry silverberry)|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425215747/http://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=ELMU|archive-date=April 25, 2013}}</ref> In [[China]], the leaves of the tree are used as a medicinal plant and a natural remedy for cough, diarrhea, itch, foul sores, and even cancer.<ref>{{cite journal|pmid=35566071|pmc=9101257 |date=2022 |last1=Bieniek |first1=A. |last2=Lachowicz-Wiśniewska |first2=S. |last3=Bojarska |first3=J. |title=The Bioactive Profile, Nutritional Value, Health Benefits and Agronomic Requirements of Cherry Silverberry (Elaeagnus multiflora Thunb.): A Review |journal=Molecules |volume=27 |issue=9 |page=2719 |doi=10.3390/molecules27092719 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

USDA classifies the shrub as a medium [[Nitrogen fixation|nitrogen fixer]] - it improves the soil.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plants of the POP Learning Orchard: Nitrogen Fixing Shrubs |url=https://www.phillyorchards.org/2024/07/30/plants-of-the-pop-learning-orchard-nitrogen-fixing-shrubs/ |access-date=2024-10-30 |website=Philadelphia Orchard Project |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Fruit composition==

The fruits contain:

11 – 18  % sugar, 

1.5 – 2.3  % organic acids,

0.18 – 0.46  % pectin, 

13.2 – 19  mg / 100 g of vitamin A, 

16 – 33  mg / 100 g vitamin C (according to other sources up to 110.6 mg%, data for the Russian variety Krylyon).<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://fialka.tomsk.ru/index.php/17-gumi|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251024033105/fialka.tomsk.ru/index.php/17-gumi|archive-date=2025-10-24|language=ru|title=Лох многоцветковый или гуми (Elaeagnus multiflora)}}</ref>

It also contains about 0.3–0.5% tannins,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://referatu.net.ua/referats/7569/156885 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170716212647/http://referatu.net.ua/referats/7569/156885 |archive-date=2017-07-16|title=web.archive.org/web/20170716212647/http://referatu.net.ua/referats/7569/156885|language=ru }}</ref> about 68  mg/kg of iron, a lot of polyphenolic compounds (about 285–765  mg %), and amino acids.<ref>{{cite web | author=Редакция журнала Наука и жизнь | title=ЛОХ ЗА КАЛИТКОЙ | website=Наука и жизнь | url=https://www.nkj.ru/archive/articles/13295/ | language=ru | access-date=2026-04-23}}</ref> They contain 17 times more lycopene than tomatoes.

==History==
It was introduced to Europe around 1850 (Netherlands). The French were the first to cultivate this fruit species in Europe around 1877, but cultivation never spread beyond a small part of the French province of Lorraine.<ref>{{cite web | title=Petit fruit vosgien : Le goumi | url=http://croqcentrevosges.free.fr/goumi.html }}</ref> The possibility of cultivation in Russia began to be investigated sometime after 1945, but more intensively only around 2000 (although the first seedlings were introduced to Russia as early as 1926).<ref name="auto"/> It has only been cultivated in America for the last 15-20 years (the first seedlings were imported to the USA about 100 years ago).<ref>Reich,L. Uncommon Fruits for Every Garden,Portland 2004.,p.115</ref>  In Poland, cultivation research began around 1995, in Ukraine around 1980.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bieniek | first1=A. | last2=Lachowicz-Wiśniewska | first2=S. | last3=Bojarska | first3=J. | title=The Bioactive Profile, Nutritional Value, Health Benefits and Agronomic Requirements of Cherry Silverberry (Elaeagnus multiflora Thunb.): A Review | journal=Molecules | date=2022 | volume=27 | issue=9 | page=2719 | doi=10.3390/molecules27092719 | doi-access=free | pmid=35566071 | pmc=9101257 }}</ref> In China, Korea and especially Japan, goumi has been a common and highly valued fruit species for centuries.

==Cultivated varieties==
* Sweet Scarlet: A red-berry Ukrainian variety popular in the United States. It is partially self-fertile, requiring another variety for pollination.

* Goumi SPP: Austrian variety, self-fertile and therefore capable of producing fruit without any other pollinator.

* Carmine: An American red-fruited variety, available in the United States. It is prized for its productivity and fruit quality.

* Yahidka: A small variety from Ukraine, ideal for small gardens or potted crops.

* Red Gem: A popular Russian variety in the United States, known for its fruit and disease resistance.

* Sakhalinskiy pervi - Russian variety

* Krilyon - Russian variety

* Moneron - Russian variety

* Taisa - Russian variety 

* Sunrise Ruby -  Korean variety<ref>{{cite web | title=Buy Sunrise Ruby (TM) Goumi Online | Burnt Ridge Nursery-Burnt Ridge Nursery | url=https://www.burntridgenursery.com/SUNRISE-RUBY-TM-GOUMI-Elaegnus-muliflora/productinfo/NSGMSUN/ }}</ref>

* Pippi - new uSA variety<ref>{{cite web | title=Introducing 'Pippi' Goumi Berries | url=https://johannsgarden.blogspot.com/2021/01/introducing-pippi-goumi-berries.html?sc=1762358144876#c990658828402009426 }}</ref>

* Gigantea (Daiougoumi): Japanese variety.Recognizable by its larger fruits (6 to 10 grams), this variety has excellent potential for hybridization and crop improvement.

* Macrocarpa: Another large-fruited variety, each fruit weighing about 3.5 grams, compared to other varieties whose fruits weigh about 1 gram.

* Bikkuri Gumi: A Japanese variety (translation "Surprise"). Possibly the same variety as Daiougoumi. The fruits appear to be even larger (10 grams)<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Гуми - лох многоцветковый |url=https://fialka.tomsk.ru/index.php/17-gumi |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251024033105/https://fialka.tomsk.ru/index.php/17-gumi |archive-date=2025-10-24 |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=fialka.tomsk.ru |language=ru-ru}}</ref>
